bindings.explanation: NodaMoney rounds during construction using the selected or ambient context; the standard path can choose currency scale. This contrasts with a generic exact-value boundary and shows why a composing rounding policy must be expressly identified.

Dinero separates its calculator from money operations. The inspected number path has precision limits and a no-progress guard; choosing a monetary library or calculator does not by itself establish exact arithmetic.

The inspected addition path checks currency compatibility before combining amounts and rejects a mismatch with both currencies identified. This supports the addition control; other comparisons and conversions were not reviewed.

py-moneyed rejects mismatched-currency addition and retains currency in new results. Its native equality returns false for different currencies, so the finding is a partial match rather than evidence for every operation in this rule.

Money PHP carries source currency and tracks residual units so successful allocation can conserve the total. It chooses recipients by fractional loss, whereas Core uses declared order; conservation does not settle that policy choice.

With FloorToFirst, positive integer weights and an explicitly matched fixed unit context, Brick allocates the source magnitude, assigns remaining steps in order and restores the sign. The selected negative cases exercise the same signed allocation approach.

RubyMoney carries the remaining amount through successive splits, with selected tests checking the final sum. This numeric helper does not establish currency preservation, and its algorithm/input domain differs from Core allocation.

The inspected Dinero distribution utility gives residual units to larger weights. For 801 units and weights [1, 3], its test expects [200, 601]; Core declared-order allocation gives [201, 600]. Both preserve the total at these small values.

GoMoney equal splitting distributes signed residual units to the first positions. Its ratio method also accepts all-zero weights and can return zeros for a nonzero source, so the broader method is not a conservation guarantee.

Moov recomputes file-to-batch and batch-to-entry totals rather than relying on structural acceptance. This payment-domain control illustrates evaluating related values together; it is not an implementation of the bounded Core Entity model.

TigerBeetle includes pending and posted counters in configured account-limit predicates before inserting a new transfer. It illustrates the importance of evaluating the complete relevant state; the ledger formula is outside Core.

ERPNext accumulates duplicate voucher and term references against fresh outstanding data. Its test rejects a combined 200 allocation against an invoice outstanding of 100, even though each individual row could appear acceptable.

The inspected allocation guards and local result construction do not assign to the source Money amount or currency when rejecting invalid ratios. This supports operand preservation in that path, not every observable financial effect in the whole library.

The inspected invoice test expects outstanding to remain 100 after an excessive aggregate payment is rejected. This is an application-domain assertion read from source; it does not prove all related state or concurrency behavior.

Formance constructs inverse postings in another transaction value. The helper alone establishes neither a verifiable original-event link nor a persisted reversal, making it a useful boundary example for this rule rather than a demonstrated match.

An omitted NodaMoney context can resolve to a global or thread-local policy and affect the constructed amount. Reproducing the outcome therefore requires identifying the applicable context; ambient lookup alone is not a portable context contract.

The selected py-moneyed rounding test changes its expected result when the active Decimal rounding context changes. This identifies a material numeric dependency, while the full arithmetic context remains unverified.

Beancount balance checks use explicit tolerance or derive it from decimal precision and an option. Those facts change assertion outcomes and must be retained for reproduction; ledger tolerance remains separate from exact Money equality.

QuantLib Actual/360 receives a declared last-day inclusion setting that changes the year fraction. This is a concrete example of material calculation context; Core does not currently define interest day-count conventions.

ERPNext validates against freshly queried outstanding values, party/account facts and configured precision. Those dependencies affect the result; refreshing facts does not alone define a stable snapshot or a concurrency guarantee.
